scalar.def: A quantity with a size (and a unit) but no direction, such as distance, speed, time or mass.

vector.def: A quantity with both a size and a direction, such as displacement or velocity. Along a line, its sign gives its direction.

magnitude.def: The size of a vector, with no direction: always zero or positive. The magnitude of a velocity of −4.2 m/s is 4.2 m/s.

position.def: Where an object is, measured from an origin along a chosen positive direction, in meters. Along a line it is one signed number, x.

coordinate-system.def: The choice of an origin (zero point) and a positive direction (an x-axis) used to give positions as numbers.

distance.def: The total length of the path an object travels: a scalar that counts every meter and never decreases.

displacement.def: The change in position: final position minus starting position. A vector; along a line its sign gives its direction.

speed.def: How fast an object moves, as a distance per time (m/s): a scalar, the magnitude of the velocity.

velocity.def: How fast an object moves and in which direction: displacement per time, in m/s. A vector; its magnitude is the speed.

vector-sum-1d.def: Adding vectors along one line by adding their signed values: +12 m and −5 m add to +7 m. The result is the resultant.
